newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish pensioners to get compensation in July.
newsitem.headline: Polish pensioners to get compensation in July.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament approved a bill on Friday which provides for compensating pensioners for pay rises they should have been granted in 1996.
Under the bill, approved in a 262 to 64 vote with 56 abstentions, pensioners will get an average pay increase of 2.8 percent in July in addition to other increases.
The payout will cost about 2.5 billion zlotys but the 1997 budget draft offers only 1.2 billion zlotys for this purpose.

The finance ministry's officials were not immediately available for comment on how to finance the remaining sum. PAP news agency reported that the 1.3 billion zlotys will be provided from the budgetary reserve.
As a result of the rise, an average pension would increase by 2.8 percent in real terms this year and not 1.5 percent as initially envisaged by the budget.
The bill still needs to clear the Senate and be signed by the president, but neither is likely to oppose it.

The payout for pensioners stems from a constitutional court ruling last year that pensions should have been increased in March, 1996, as was envisaged by the social security law which was effective until the end of 1995.

The law was changed as of January last year as a prelude to a planned social security reform and the new legislation offered pensioners a 2.5 percent real pay increase in 1996, to be made in September. The Tribunal, which decides whether laws are compatible with the constitution, ruled that the pensions rise should have been granted in March because it was linked to wage growth in the last quarter of 1995, when the old law was still effective.
